# Space Bunny fixed-input scientific screen: failed

**Classification:** local design choice; no claim about Google's private implementation or expert validation. **Decision:** the selected `openrouter/stealth/space-bunny-alpha` configuration is **unqualified on the frozen scientific screen**. It remains an observed zero-price operational route, but one completed public run is not evidence of repeatable claim assessment.

The owner authorized resuming the bounded comparison on 27 September. The [committed protocol](m12-space-bunny-scientific-protocol-2026-09-27.md) pinned the production assessor, four public claims, request policy and stop rule. The product and evaluator Git objects match its base commit `b7e9a0d3260cb769e17561e7ab3a415756907619`; runner and input SHA-256 values still match the protocol. OpenRouter's [model page](https://openrouter.ai/stealth/space-bunny-alpha) listed Space Bunny as free, its [billing FAQ](https://openrouter.ai/support/) described provider-pass-through inference pricing without a request fee, and the exact endpoint API returned one Stealth endpoint at zero prompt/completion price immediately before each actual trial. Both requests pinned Stealth, disabled fallbacks and sent zero price ceilings. The existing key authenticated; no credential was retained in these artifacts.

| Stage | Physical requests | Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Initial launcher preflight | 0 | The script path omitted the repository from `PYTHONPATH`, so import failed before artifact creation or inference. Corrected only the launcher environment; production code and frozen runner were unchanged. | [aborted launch](baseline/model-qualification/space-bunny-batch-aborted-launch-2026-09-27.json) |
| Four-claim trial 1 | 1 | `partial`, `supports`, `insufficient`, `contradicts` in order. Each cited quote matched its frozen passage and offsets; `model_primary` or `lexical_founded` method, with no deterministic fallback. | [trial](baseline/model-qualification/space-bunny-batch-trial1-2026-09-27.json), [price and account snapshot](baseline/model-qualification/space-bunny-batch-trial1-launch-2026-09-27.json) |
| Four-claim trial 2 | 1 | Failed. The served model returned JSON with `"verdests"` instead of the required `"verdicts"`. The production parser found no verdicts and fell back deterministically on all four claims; three resulting labels differed from the gold labels. The received JSON's apparent labels are not the product's observed output. | [trial](baseline/model-qualification/space-bunny-batch-trial2-2026-09-27.json), [price and account snapshot](baseline/model-qualification/space-bunny-batch-trial2-launch-2026-09-27.json) |

Each actual response reported served model `stealth/space-bunny-alpha`, complete usage and `$0` cost; the authenticated account usage fields were unchanged across each before/after snapshot. These observations are not a separate billing audit. Trial 1 and trial 2 used fresh processes, disabled evaluator caching and exactly one observed physical request each. Both launch receipts record the source commit and zero-price endpoint check. Trial 2 exited 0 because a deterministic fallback is valid product behavior, but the predeclared scientific acceptance gate rejects fallback and incorrect labels. The protocol's first-failed-trial rule therefore stopped the series: **no trial 3 or 30-item citation panel was run**. No threshold, parser, assessor or evaluation input was changed to rescue the result.

The predeclared first-failure stop closes this selected-route screen as failed: Space Bunny is unqualified under its criteria, while broader scientific quality remains inconclusive. It does not qualify a replacement default or dispose of the separate result-conditioned novelty candidate. Any proposed model or product correction needs a new, frozen protocol and its own evidence; trial 2 must remain in the record.
